Scaled Schoenfeld Residuals of the Treatment Effect

Source: R/plot_schoenfeld.R
plot_schoenfeld.Rd

For each arm other than the control arm, fits a Cox model to the data of the two arms and plots the scaled Schoenfeld residuals of the treatment effect (survival::cox.zph()) against time with:

  • the estimated log hazard ratio of the Cox model (pink line);

  • the regression of the residuals on time (black line), a natural cubic spline with 4 degrees of freedom as in survival::plot.cox.zph(), with its pointwise confidence interval (dotted lines);

  • the log hazard ratio and the p-value of the Grambsch-Therneau test of test_proportional_hazards, in the title of the panel.

A flat regression line close to the log hazard ratio indicates that the treatment effect does not depend on time, that is, proportional hazards.

Usage

plot_schoenfeld(
  data,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  time_unit = c("months", "days", "weeks", "years"),
  legend_position = c("bottom", "right", "top", "left", "none"),
  colours = NULL,
  linetypes = NULL,
  text_sizes = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Data frame returned by processing_dataset, with two or more treatment arms.

conf_level

Confidence level of the interval of the regression line, a single number in (0, 1). The default is 0.95.

time_unit

Time unit of the data: "months" (the default), "days", "weeks" or "years".

legend_position

Position of the legend: "bottom" (the default), "right", "top", "left" or "none".

colours

NULL (the default) or colours of the elements of the plot: "residuals" (points, dark blue), "log_hr" (estimated log hazard ratio, pink), "regression" (regression on time, black) and "confidence_interval" (black). A named vector sets the colours of the elements it names; an unnamed vector gives the four colours in this order.

linetypes

NULL (the default) or line types of "log_hr" (solid), "regression" (solid) and "confidence_interval" (dotted), given as for colours (see plot_km for the line types).

text_sizes

NULL (the default) or a named vector of font sizes in points, with some or all of the names "title" (titles of the plot and of its panels), "axis_title", "axis_text", "legend" and "risk_table" (numbers at risk and names of the arms below the plot; the title of the table is 1.125 times as large). The texts not named keep their default sizes: 14 points for the axis titles, 16.8 for the title of a plot, and 11.2 for the titles of panels, the axis text, the legend and the numbers at risk.

Value

A ggplot object (one panel per comparison with the control arm, titled with the comparison, the log hazard ratio and the p-value).

Details

The scaled residuals are centred on the log hazard ratio (they estimate the time-varying coefficient beta(t)), so the reference line is the estimated log hazard ratio and not 0. The confidence interval of the regression uses the variance returned by cox.zph(), as in plot.cox.zph(), with the normal quantile of conf_level.

References

Grambsch PM, Therneau TM (1994). Proportional hazards tests and diagnostics based on weighted residuals. Biometrika 81(3):515-526. doi:10.1093/biomet/81.3.515

Examples

dat <- processing_dataset(
  system.file("extdata", "fit_example.csv", package = "SurvFitSummary"),
  column_arm = "TRT01P", column_survtime = "AVAL", column_cnsr = "CNSR",
  control_arm = "Control"
)
plot_schoenfeld(dat)
